newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeri industry shows signs of new growth.
newsitem.headline: Azeri industry shows signs of new growth.

text.p: Azeri industrial output rose in February for the first time since the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991 and officials on Wednesday said the economy was finally on track for growth.

The country, located on the Caspian Sea where it is actively developing major oil fields in cooperation with major Western producers, saw industrial output rise 2.1 percent year-on-year after a 16.6 percent fall in the previous year.

"The growth of output indicates that the country's economy stabilisation which started in the second half of last year is moving ahead," said Meri Gardashkhanova, head of Statistic Information Department at the State Socioeconomic Committee.

She said industrial output growth was aided by a five percent rise in metallurgical production, a six percent rise in the construction materials sector and a 7.8 percent rise in machine building output.
A slump in the light and petrochemical sectors had stopped, she said.
Azeri gross domestic product rose four percent year-on-year in February and consumer price inflation slowed to 0.6 percent month-on-month from 1.7 percent in January.
An Economy Ministry spokesman said that the fuel and energy sector was the mainstay of the economy, accounting for 60-65 percent of GDP in 1996.
